concept: one_line: The map is a hinged strip of six regions, and two regions become neighbours when a hinge is folded so a post on one seats into a socket on the other — distance is a shape you put the world into, not a line drawn on it. | slug: fold-line | arm: modular-worldbuild | emotion: vertigo — the map you were planning across stops being the map the second somebody else folds it | piggyback: pawn movement across a connected map plus a visit-all-four goal (pick-up-and-deliver's shape) | audience: adults 14+ who like route games and puzzle objects — Ticket to Ride players who own a Rubik's cube — and anyone who has thought a game board was too static a thing; never children | players 2-4, light, target_minutes 30 | fun_correct_bet: the winning line is folding the world into a shape where your next two hops exist and your rivals' next hop does not, and then daring them to spend their turn undoing it. Ignore the geometry and you sit in a region that connects to nothing. | nearest_known: Ticket to Ride and Pandemic (fixed graph, moving pawns); origami puzzle objects and folding-map toys (a shape, never a game). I know of no published board game where folding the board is the move.
mechanism: Six printed terrain plates, 100 x 100 x 8 mm, joined in a strip by five printed knuckle hinges with snap pins that detent hard at 0, 90 and 180 degrees. Each plate carries three posts (12 mm tall, keyed triangle/square/round) and three matching sockets, positioned so that folding a hinge to 90 degrees seats certain posts of one plate into sockets of a plate two or three positions away — a seated post IS a bridge, and it is either seated or it is not, with a click you can hear. Four of the plates hold a printed shrine. Turn: either move your runner one step to any region connected to it — adjacent along the strip, or bridged by a seated post — or refold exactly one hinge by one detent. Refolding is the whole knife: any bridge it breaks is gone, and a runner standing on a plate whose only connection just vanished is not sent home, it is simply stuck until someone folds it back. Two runners may never occupy the same region; arriving bumps the sitting runner one step along the strip. Goal: touch all four shrines and return your runner to the plate you started on. First runner home wins; if a full round passes with no move and no fold, whoever has touched the most shrines wins.
physical_hook: Cardboard breaks: adjacency here is created by two solids meeting in the air above the table when the map is bent out of the plane — a cardboard board that folds just gets smaller, and 'plate 2 now touches plate 5' cannot be printed on a flat sheet because in the plane it is false. Molding breaks: the game is five snap-pin hinges with 90-degree detents tuned to hold a plate's weight without creeping, plus keyed post/socket pairs at a 0.2 mm interference so a bridge is felt and heard, and each copy is printed with a different post-and-socket map so every buyer's fold puzzle is its own; a mould gives one fixed fold graph and cannot chase detent stiffness batch to batch.
title: Fold Line
